# relay_backup_schedule (Resource)

The backup schedule of a managed PostgreSQL or Valkey cluster. Every apply replaces the whole schedule, so an attribute left out takes the platform's value. Destroying the resource resets the cluster to the platform default schedule; it does not turn backups off. Only the attributes set in the configuration are tracked for drift. The cluster must have backups enabled. A cluster still on the platform default has no schedule to import.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "relay_backup_schedule" "orders" {
  workspace_id     = relay_workspace.prod.id
  cluster_id       = relay_postgresql_cluster.orders.id
  snapshot_time    = { hour = 3, minute = 30 }
  pitr_window_days = 14

  tiers = [
    { frequency = "hourly", interval = 6, retention_value = 8 },
    { frequency = "daily", interval = 1, retention_value = 7 },
    { frequency = "weekly", interval = 1, retention_value = 4 },
    { frequency = "monthly", interval = 1, retention_value = 12 },
  ]
}

resource "relay_backup_schedule" "sessions" {
  workspace_id  = relay_workspace.prod.id
  cluster_id    = relay_valkey_cluster.sessions.id
  snapshot_time = { hour = 4, minute = 0 }
  max_backups   = 7
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) `relay_postgresql_cluster` or `relay_valkey_cluster` ID.
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace of the cluster.

### Optional

- `max_backups` (Number) Full backups kept when `tiers` is not set; the platform default is 4. With tiers, the weekly tier's retention decides and the API ignores this value, so the two conflict.
- `pitr_window_days` (Number) Requested point-in-time-restore window in days, PostgreSQL only; the platform default is 7. Valkey restores are snapshot-only, so a Valkey cluster rejects it.
- `snapshot_time` (Attributes) UTC wall-clock time the daily, weekly and monthly tiers fire at. Defaults to 02:00. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--snapshot_time))
- `tiers` (Attributes List) Retention ladder, at most one tier per frequency. Every enabled tier is rendered into the cluster's backup crons and retention counts; the weekly tier takes the full backup and the daily tier the incremental one. Left out, the cluster takes a weekly full and a daily incremental backup, each kept `max_backups` times. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tiers))

### Read-Only

- `active_backups` (Number) Backups currently retained.
- `id` (String) The cluster ID.
- `last_backup_time` (String) Completion time of the last backup, RFC 3339, empty before the first one.
- `next_backup_time` (String) Next scheduled backup, RFC 3339.
- `platform_default` (Boolean) Always false while Terraform manages the schedule. A schedule reset to the default outside Terraform is removed from state.

<a id="nestedatt--snapshot_time"></a>
### Nested Schema for `snapshot_time`

Required:

- `hour` (Number) Hour, 0 to 23.
- `minute` (Number) Minute, 0 to 59.


<a id="nestedatt--tiers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tiers`

Required:

- `frequency` (String) `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`.
- `interval` (Number) For `hourly`, the spacing in hours, a divisor of 24. For `weekly`, the weekday, 1 (Sunday) to 7 (Saturday). For `monthly`, the day of the month, 1 to 31, or 40 for the last day, which currently runs on the 28th. Ignored for `daily`.
- `retention_value` (Number) How many backups of this tier are kept, at least 1.

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Defaults to true. A disabled tier is stored but takes no backups.
- `retention_unit` (String) Implied by the frequency: `days` for hourly and daily, `weeks` for weekly, `months` for monthly.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import relay_backup_schedule.orders <workspace_id>/<cluster_id>
```
